questions.problem:
Consider the affine transformation $T$ defined as

$$
x=2v+u+1,\,y=u-v-2.
$$

Let $A$ be the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T.$

Which of the following statements are true?

- $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]$
- $det(A)=-3$
- The transformation $T$ is orientation-preserving
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Let's look at each statement in turn:

- Statement I is false. Notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2v+u+1 \\ u-v-2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u+2v \\ u-v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T$ is $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].$

- Statement II is true. Indeed, computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|=1\cdot (-1)-2\cdot 1=-3.
$$

- Statement III is false. Since $det(A)<0,$ the affine transformation $T$ is not orientation-preserving.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

questions.problem:
Consider the affine transformation $T$ defined as

$$
x=2v-u+2,\,y=2u+v-5.
$$

Let $A$ be the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T.$

Which of the following statements are true?

- $A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]$
- $det(A)=-5$
- The transformation $T$ is orientation-preserving
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Let's look at each statement in turn:

- Statement I is true. Indeed, notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2v-u+2 \\ 2u+v-5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-u+2v \\ 2u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T$ is $A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].$

- Statement II is true. Indeed, computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|=(-1)\cdot 1-2\cdot 2=-5.
$$

- Statement III is false. Since $det(A)<0,$ the affine transformation $T$ is not orientation-preserving.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14114754/assets/79b09bcf02998adf6d7bf19e7d59cabdc563ff26266966440bbb49be53029ac3.png)

Consider the triangle $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 1,\,-\frac{u+1}{2}\le v\le u+1}.
$$

The transformation $T$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following gives the image of $Δ$ in the $xy$-plane under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation is already in matrix form 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & ={{[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $T$ maps the boundary of $Δ$ to the boundary of the image. So, to find the image of $Δ,$ we find the images of each side.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14114754/assets/539c74bf4d397916fd7ac11089fa9500bd71cdf2278891136785d6e792431b05.png)

             

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing all vertices of our triangle:

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $b$ in each column:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

The image of $u$ under $T$ is given by $Au+b.$ So, by applying $T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertices of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(-1,-1),(1,-1),$ and $(-2,2).$

Drawing this region in the $xy$-plane, we get the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14114754/assets/adfe476bd2ca719996d612855ca5368bdea09370b7befcffb08a062db8587cbb.png)

          

Finally, since $det(A)=-1<0,$ this transformation is not orientation-preserving.
